messages:
mira: heads-up — overnight perf CI flagged a p95 jump on the small-batch benchmark (job: sb-small, ~03:12 UTC). spike only on GPU nodes with 80+ concurrent requests, looks like token tail latency. attaching short log excerpt and artifact link. can someone take a look when they wake up?
perf-ci-bot: Alert: p95 latency increased 42% for sb-small on pool=gpu-preemptible. Job: sb-small/2026-03-17T03:12. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/sb-small/3419998765
alex: @mira thanks — can you paste the commit sha and the test matrix (model, seq_len, batch) here?
mira: sure — sha: d4f7a9b2, model: redwood-13b/quantized, seq_len: 128, batch: 8, concurrency: 85. repro job id: sb-small-3419998765. log snippet: ```2026-03-17T03:12:27Z [runner] p95=141ms (baseline 98ms) ; tail outliers at token 10-12```
sam: thanks. i'll kick off a local repro with that sha + config. can you confirm whether KV cache reuse was enabled? iirc we flipped a cache flag in the patch.
mira: yes we enabled kv_cache_reuse=true in runtime flags for that rollout.
alex: if kv cache reuse is on, could be KV eviction thrash under high concurrency. sam if you repro, try toggling kv_cache_reuse=false and see delta. also pull perf profile with `--capture-kernels`.
oncall-ryan: i'm on pager but free to hold the node for 10m if you need to run a live profile — ping me when you want it.
sam: repro started locally, kicking with `./ci/run_perf --job=sb-small --sha=d4f7a9b2 --concurrency=85 --capture-kernels`. if kv_cache_reuse=false the p95 looks back to ~100ms in initial run. with reuse=true it's consistently ~140ms. uploading traces now.
mira: that's helpful — so reuse flips it. does that imply an eviction policy problem or a cost in cache lookups? alex any quick thoughts on which layer to instrument?
alex: likely a contention in the KV cache metadata lock; please run `perf record -g` on the runtime PID and send the flamegraph. also check kernel context-switches (`pidstat -w`) to see syscall spikes.
sam: flamegraph attached: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/sb-small/3419998765/flamegraph.svg — shows heavy time in `kv_cache::lookup` -> `mutex::lock` and a few GPU sync points.
mira: ok — looks like mutex hot path. can we try a config patch that switches to sharded cache locks as a quick canary? sam/alex can we test a sharded-cache build on the same job?
alex: i'll spin a sharded-lock build and push an image to `ci/redwood/perf-canary:sharded-3419998765`. sam can you run sb-small against that image (same params)?
sam: running now. `./ci/run_perf --image=ci/redwood/perf-canary:sharded-3419998765 --job=sb-small --sha=d4f7a9b2 --concurrency=85`. initial p95 is 105ms — much closer to baseline.
mira: awesome. can we keep the canary running for an hour, then promote as a patch to the nightly fleet if stable? also i'd like a short PR with the sharded-lock change and a perf test added to catch this.
onal: :eyes: (reaction)
oncall-ryan: leaving node held for another 20m. lmk when you finish.
alex: i'll open the PR and add the new perf regression test to the nightly matrix. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6422. note: needs review from eng-runtime and eng-ml since cache semantics touch correctness.
mira: thanks everyone — i'll update the incident tracker and add a postmortem note. tagging this as resolved for now since canary looks good. follow-ups: (1) code review for sharded locks, (2) add an alert rule to surface kv_cache mutex contention (via perf counters), (3) regression test in nightly with concurrency=85.
sam: filed a short runbook snippet in the repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/blob/main/ops/runbooks/kv-cache-hotlock.md
alex: thanks — great coordination. :thumbsup:
